Apple has cited a recently stayed securities fraud lawsuit in support of its request to halt further district court proceedings in its legal battle with Epic Games, while awaiting Supreme Court review of part of the dispute. Details below.

Apple cites related ruling — Judge Rogers reviewing request for stay

Earlier this year, a proposed class action on behalf of the City of Coral Springs Police Officers Pension Plan was filed against Apple, alleging securities fraud.

The lawsuit accuses Apple of misleading investors about whether the company had truly complied with the injunction in the Epic Games case, and whether it would deliver on a previously announced AI-powered Siri feature.

Meanwhile, Apple is continuing to challenge a finding of civil contempt in the Epic case. The Supreme Court is now reviewing whether Apple could face a civil contempt ruling over the commissions it charges on purchases made outside the App Store — a 2021 injunction requires Apple to allow outside purchasing options but did not explicitly prohibit such fees.

Last week, Apple asked the district court to stay proceedings to determine what commissions, if any, Apple can charge on purchases outside the App Store, while the Supreme Court reviews the contempt finding.

Apple argued the Supreme Court's ruling could affect district court proceedings, a claim Epic Games disputes.

In fact, Apple had previously filed a similar request to stay the Coral Springs securities fraud case, because it also involves the Epic Games dispute.

Earlier, Judge Noël Wise granted Apple's request, meaning the Coral Springs case will remain on hold until the Supreme Court decides on the civil contempt ruling.

That ruling has now prompted Apple to file Judge Wise's decision in the Epic Games case with the court, arguing the decision supports its request to Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers to stay proceedings.

Excerpted from Apple's petition filed with Judge Rogers:

Judge Rogers is now reviewing Apple's arguments in favor of, and Epic's arguments against, staying the case. Apple is hoping Judge Wise's decision will convince Judge Rogers to do the same.

Notably, in its reply opposing Epic's objection to staying the case, Apple also asked Judge Gonzalez Rogers to administratively hold proceedings even if she denies the stay request, so that Apple may seek a continued freeze from the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals or the Supreme Court while the high court separately reviews the contempt ruling.
